text: What is winter blend gasoline? Cheaper fuel sold outside summer months. Winter blend gasoline is a gasoline formula that filling stations may sell outside the summer season, which runs from June 1 to Sept. 15 under federal rules. It is cheaper to produce than summer blend, so pump prices often fall in the autumn.. Oil prices fell to their lowest since late August after Trump said the Iran war was "effectively over," and US pump prices dropped below $4 a gallon as stations switched to winter blend fuel.. The summer blend is designed to guard against evaporation, which matters in hot weather. Federal rules require stations to sell it from June 1 to Sept. 15. Outside that period, stations may switch to the winter blend, which costs less to make. The switch is one reason pump prices slipped this month. The national average for regular gasoline fell to $3.9788 a gallon on Tuesday, Nov. 10, according to AAA, the first time below $4 since July 20. It had been $4.56 earlier this year. AAA says prices typically fall 10 to 30 cents a gallon during the winter months, partly because demand drops as people take fewer road trips. Crude oil also contributed. Brent crude fell to $89.66 a barrel on Tuesday morning in London, its lowest since Aug. 31, after President Donald Trump said the war with Iran was "effectively over." Brent had peaked at $113.43 on Oct. 30. Gas prices remain more than 30% above their level before the war began on Feb. 28.
